items.author: andunie
items.descZh: 该项目源于开发者对 LocalSend 和 DashBeam 等现有跨设备传输工具低效体验的不满，旨在重塑高效、快捷的文件传输方案。核心功能聚焦于极致的传输速度，并创新性地引入了 Slint 框架进行开发，以探索更优的客户端性能。最大的亮点在于，它不仅能实现快速传输，还能与外部可信用户建立一个可“始终保持在线”的持久化通信通道，突破了传统点对点传输的临时性限制。该产品特别适用于需要与特定外部信任方保持长期、稳定且高频数据交互的个人及专业工作场景。

items.author: dvrp
items.descZh: 该产品是一种创新工具，旨在将普通的JavaScript代码直接转换为功能完整的神经网络模型。其核心功能在于无需任何训练过程，即可实现精确且完全可微分的运算，并且能够在浏览器环境中流畅运行，无需依赖GPU硬件。亮点包括具体性能指标，如示例中展示的权重数量达9,909个、网络层数为130层、训练次数为0，同时支持将条件语句等代码结构转换为ReLU激活函数形式，确保高效并行处理。适用场景广泛，涵盖从构建小型操作系统、实时训练交互式画廊，到加速搜索100,000个JSON文档等多种应用。
items.quote: 将常规 JavaScript 代码转变为神经网络。无需训练，精确且完全可微分，无需 GPU 即可在浏览器中运行。

items.author: hfshfg
items.descZh: MoneySwitch 是一个专为 AI Agent 打造的可编程、自托管 Web3 云钱包项目，旨在为人工智能自主经济提供安全、可控的支付基础设施。其核心功能是“给 AI 一把资金 API 密钥”，通过引入 MoneyKeys、预算限制（budgets）和审批机制（approvals），实现对 agent 支付权限的精细化管控。技术上，该项目基于高性能的 Monad 网络，结合 x402 支付协议与 USDC 稳定币，构建了低延迟、低成本的链上自动化支付通道。项目提供完整的自托管部署方案（如 Docker Compose）及配套的技能插件与工具集，降低了开发者集成 AI 支付功能的门槛。该方案非常适用于 AI 自主调用付费 API、链上微支付结算、自动化云资源采购等需要 Agent 拥有独立且受控资金支配能力的前沿业务场景。
items.quote: 给你的 AI 一个 API 密钥来赚钱。

items.title: Show HN: Portal – Native Ghostty and Web View as Emacs Buffers
items.desc: description: A portal from Emacs to the rest of the computer: native macOS views inside Emacs panes. title: Portal image: https://unclex.net/assets/coverDaKkqAd.png Overview Portal is, as the name suggests, a portal from Emacs to the rest of the computer. It puts native macOS views inside Emacs panes, so a buffer can show a real web page or a real terminal as if it were ordinary buffer content. Four Emacs panes: GitHub in a web view, Excalidraw, a rendered Markdown file and a Ghostty terminal There are two kinds of view: Web view the system WebKit view, and with it everything the web can do. Terminal view a native Ghostty terminal. That's it. Portal is a set of primitives. The things I built on top (Excalidraw, Markdown and HTML previews, quick terminals) are my preferences, and they're small on purpose. The primitives are the point: you can build your own things on them. Why I wanted to stay in Emacs. Emacs can't do everything a browser or a terminal app can, and the inEmacs alternatives (xwidgetwebkit, terminal emulators drawn with Emacs text) are slow or don't work well on macOS. Instead of bringing those things into Emacs text, Portal puts the real native views in the pane and lets Emacs manage them. Install Portal needs GNU Emacs 31.1 or newer, built for macOS's graphical NS interface with dynamic modules, plus Swift 6.2+ (Xcode), CMake and Ninja. Bun is optional; the build fetches a pinned one if you don't have it. Add it to your config: emacslisp (usepackage portal :vc (:url "https://github.com/xiaoxinghu/portal" :rev :newest)) Then Mx portalabout. The first time, Portal offers to build its native part, which downloads a pinned GhosttyKit, so no Zig is needed. Run portalabout again once it's ready and you should see an animated portal in a native web view, with your Portal and Emacs versions. Click it or press RET to enter it, ⌘. to come back to Emacs. The [install guide](https://github.com/xiaoxinghu/portal/blob/main/docs/install.md) covers straight.el, building from a clone, and troubleshooting. Views Every view follows the same rules, whatever renders it: A buffer has at most one view. The view shows up in whichever pane displays the buffer, and follows it through splits, resizes and frames. Hiding the buffer hides the view; it doesn't stop it. Pages keep running, terminal sessions keep their processes. Killing the buffer closes it. The keyboard is handed over explicitly. Enter a view and it behaves like a macOS app; chords it doesn't use fall through to Emacs, and ⌘. gives the keyboard back. Because the view belongs to a buffer, everything Emacs already does with buffers (displaybuffer rules, consultbuffer, window layouts) works on web pages and terminals too. Web View The web view is the system WKWebView, the engine Safari uses. It loads any http, https, file or data URL: emacslisp (portalopenurl "https://example.com") (portalrenderhtml "mockup.html") (portalrendermarkdown "PLAN.md") Behind it is a small Bun server, the app host. Emacs starts it on demand, one per Emacs process, bound to localhost with a fresh access token. It ships as a standalone binary, so you don't need Bun or Node at runtime. Pages served by the app host are _hosted apps_, and they get a bridge to their buffer: the page posts JSON with window.portalBridge.postMessage, Emacs receives it as plists, and portalwebsend sends messages back. A web UI can talk to Emacs directly, without a server of its own. What I built on top of it: Excalidraw offline, editing .excalidraw files. Emacs owns opening and saving; the drawing is just a buffer. Markdown preview rendered by the app host, with a table of contents and an Open in Emacs button. Agents write a lot of Markdown with tables, and a web view reads them better than any Markdown mode I've tried. HTML preview any local HTML file, next to the code. Agents hand me mockups as single HTML files, often interactive, and I don't need the browser to look at them. Terminal View The terminal view is Ghostty, through GhosttyKit, rendered natively in the pane. Emacs doesn't draw a single character of it, which is why it feels like Ghostty and not like a terminal emulated inside Emacs. The primitive is just "a Ghostty terminal in a buffer". From Lisp you can run any program in one: emacslisp (portalterminalstart (expandfilename "~/code/site") "claude" '()) What I built on top of it: portalterminal for a shell in the current pane, terminals grouped by project, a quick scratch terminal per project in a panel at the bottom of the frame, Consult and Embark integration, and themes set from Elisp. Limitations macOS only, verified on Apple Silicon with macOS 27\. The native side is a C core over a Swift backend; the core is written so another platform (GTK, maybe) could implement the same primitives, but none does today. The module runs inside the Emacs process. A bug in it can crash Emacs, so try it in emacs Q first, and restart Emacs after rebuilding a module it has already loaded. Hosted apps keep no cookies or storage between sessions, and never leave the app host. Other sites open in the default browser. \\<20261012 Mon[Introducing Portal](/writing/portal) \\[Mx](/projects/mx):macos:swift: The bridge between macOS and Emacs world via callback URL. [← All projects](/projects)
items.author: xiaoxing
items.descZh: Portal 是一款针对 macOS 深度定制的 Emacs 扩展，旨在解决传统 Emacs 内嵌浏览器和文本终端运行缓慢、体验割裂的痛点，通过将真正的原生 macOS 视图直接嵌入 Emacs 窗格，实现了“编辑器即操作系统”的无缝工作流。其核心功能包括基于系统 WebKit 的原生 Web 视图和基于 GhosttyKit 的原生终端视图，两者皆非 Emacs 模拟绘制，保证了极致的原生性能，例如终端视图中 Emacs 不绘制任何字符，带来完全真实的 Ghostty 体验。亮点在于其创新的双向通信与缓冲区集成机制：通过本地 localhost 的 Bun 应用宿主以安全令牌隔离网页，并允许网页通过 JSON 消息直接与 Emacs 通信，同时视图完美融入 Emacs 的窗口拆分、隐藏与布局逻辑。键盘控制权支持显式无缝切换，非原生快捷键可透传至 Emacs，为用户提供了安全且高效的交互体验。该工具适用于需要高度集中于 Emacs 生态、同时频繁进行网页浏览、交互式 HTML 原型编辑、项目级快速终端管理以及离线绘图（如 Excalidraw）的深度开发者。
items.quote: 与其把那些东西带入 Emacs 文本，Portal 会把真实的原生视图放在窗格中，并让 Emacs 来管理它们。

Bokal bundles ExtPay, which is copyleft (AGPL3.0orlater), so the combined work is conveyed under GPLcompatible terms — a permissive license like MIT would not be compliant. Reasoning in [docs/licensingnotes.md](/yuvibabbardev/bokal/blob/main/docs/licensingnotes.md); dependency licenses in [THIRDPARTYNOTICES.md](/yuvibabbardev/bokal/blob/main/THIRDPARTYNOTICES.md). What Bokal is Bokal is a Manifest V3 cookie manager built around a single promise: your cookies never leave your device. No server, no account, no telemetry, no analytics, no remote code. It reads and writes cookies through Chrome's cookies API and does everything locally. It's aimed at web developers debugging sessions and auth, QA engineers juggling multiple accounts and login states, and privacyconscious users who want to see and control what sites store. Features (all free) Full cookie control — view, add, edit, and delete cookies, including HttpOnly cookies that UIonly tools can't touch. Se
items.author: bolalapp
items.descZh: Bokal 是一款为 Chrome 浏览器 Manifest V3 架构设计的开源 Cookie 管理器，旨在解决新版扩展 API 对 Cookie 操作限制的问题，同时确保用户数据完全本地化。它提供完整的 Cookie 生命周期管理，包括查看、添加、编辑和删除，特别支持普通 UI 工具无法触及的 HttpOnly Cookie，并内置 CHIPS 分区检查器以应对现代隐私分区策略。亮点在于无需请求 "tabs" 权限，完全本地运行，无遥测、无远程代码加载，所有操作均通过 Chrome 原生 cookies API 完成，且支持一键导出为 Playwright 或 Puppeteer 脚本以提升自动化测试效率。该工具主要面向 Web 开发者调试会话与认证流程、QA 工程师管理多账户登录状态，以及任何希望透明控制站点存储数据的隐私敏感型用户。项目以 GPL3.0 或更高版本开源，并已在 Chrome Web Store 和 Microsoft Edge Addons 上线。
items.quote: 一个适用于 Chrome (Manifest V3) 的可信赖的开源 Cookie 管理器。
items.titleZh: Show HN：Bokal – 无需“标签页”权限的开源 Cookie 编辑器

items.descZh: 作者长期以来一直想要构建一个类似于虚幻引擎蓝图、但适用于其喜爱语言的通用可视化脚本程序，尽管过往多次尝试未果，但最终借助AI技术得以成功实现。该工具的核心功能是提供跨语言的通用可视化编程能力，通过直观的图形化节点连接，帮助开发者简化复杂逻辑的编写过程。AI技术的深度集成不仅大幅提升了工具的开发效率，还赋予了其出色的易用性，让创作者能够打造出真正符合高效工作流的智能辅助工具。虽然原文未提供具体的量化性能指标，但该工具通过智能化手段显著降低了多语言编程的复杂度，实现了工作流的优化。它适用于多语言跨平台开发、游戏逻辑可视化设计，以及需要降低编码门槛、提升团队协作效率的开发者和设计人员。
